# 水彩邮记

Project adaptation of pamler1004/postmark, watercolor mode. Original skill and MIT license are preserved in upstream/. This file is the self-contained image prompt used by the app; no external files or tools are required during image generation.

## Source fidelity

Read the supplied photograph first. Preserve its main subject, recognizable architecture, clothing, pose, horizon, lighting mood, meaningful signs, and spatial relationships. Repaint the photograph into watercolor; do not paste an unmodified photograph inside a decorative border. Do not substitute a famous landmark, invent a location, alter cultural identity, or add unrelated people.

## Watercolor medium

Use soft transparent washes, wet-on-wet blending, gentle color bleeds and blooms, visible brush strokes, delicate pencil or fine ink accents on key contours. Let the paper shine through sky, water and distant shapes. Keep convincing source-derived color relationships, luminous edges and atmospheric depth. Use neutral watercolor paper with fine fibers, matte absorption grain and slight ink-density variation throughout the scene. No automatic sepia, yellowing, brown cast, grime, heavy aging, plastic surfaces or photographic filter effect.

## Postcard composition

Produce one flat, finished vertical 3:5 artwork, directly facing the viewer. Build a watercolor commemorative-stamp composition inside the canvas, with a cream perforated paper edge and optional fine painted keyline. Keep its outer edge about 4% of the canvas short side from every canvas edge. The scene is the dominant visual event. Preserve source orientation relationships through recomposition, never stretch or crop away the key subject.

Use minimal information density, subtle ornament and a bottom-band title as the default. A short hero-overlay title is allowed only when the scene has clear negative space. Use exactly one title mode and one shared alignment axis for the title group. Avoid elaborate borders, repeated stamps, floating labels and multiple frames. The host app supplies editable message, date and postage, so omit denomination, cancellation mark, serial number, issue year and official postal claims in this adaptation.

## Typography and truth

Use one short title of 2–5 words, or 2–6 Chinese characters when the user supplies Chinese text. Match a supplied exact title; otherwise choose a quiet scene-derived poetic title. Place it in the paper band, in a refined serif (Song for Chinese), with the darkest scene ink and generous breathing room. Do not add a second paragraph, fake handwriting, decorative gibberish or duplicate translations. Do not invent countries, coordinates, historical facts or personal signatures. A supplied verified location can replace the poetic title. Existing meaningful signs remain part of the scene and are not rewritten as invented brands.

## Visual check

One recognizable scene; true watercolor repaint; coherent paper and perforation; readable short title; aligned margins; no fabricated metadata; no extra postcard back, device mockup, desktop props or comparison panel.

# 木版旅绘

Project adaptation of cakeni/ukiyoe-picture-skill v1.2. Original rules and MIT license are preserved in upstream/. This self-contained prompt fixes the output to one postcard illustration.

## Visual DNA

Use flat woodblock color masses, clear hand-carved dark ink contours, simplified shadows, restrained washi fibers and softly faded pigment. Keep one main visual event with two to five supporting source-derived elements. Favor calm negative space, asymmetric balance and an inset clipped-corner dark print frame with an ivory paper margin. No photorealism, glossy 3D, cinematic lighting, lens flare, modern anime, watercolor bleeds, oil impasto or dirty grunge.

## Preserve the source

Keep the original subject placement, horizon, direction of movement, dominant occlusions, architecture, clothing and recognizable silhouettes. Preserve daytime versus night and broad color relationships. Translate every region—including clouds, reflections, grass and water—into printmaking shapes instead of laying paper texture over photography. Do not add narrative objects, replace a person, or change cultural identity: Chinese buildings remain Chinese, European roofs remain European, and modern vehicles retain their structure. Do not insert torii, cherry blossoms or Japanese text by default.

## Composition selection

Choose one source-compatible structure: architecture framed by existing foliage; quiet water and sky; source window or doorway framing; an off-center figure; a horizontal vehicle crossing landscape; a large quiet sky above a small subject; axial architecture; a portrait with one botanical cue already in the scene; or three to five overlapping mountain/water planes. Preserve spatial anchors over forcing a template. For travel, support the movement with existing rails, roads, water or mountain ridges. Do not combine all structures or make a multi-panel collage.

## Palette and surface

Limit the image to four to seven colors, approximately 70% main/background, 20% deep structural color and 10% accent. Choose source-related muted indigo, blue-gray, moss green, ivory, dusty pink or rust. Vermilion is a restrained accent, not a full red wash. Keep neutral ivory clean, with delicate washi fibers and slightly uneven ink. Use at most two subtle print effects, such as bokashi sky gradation or mild plate misregistration. No heavy grain, scratches, dust, sepia blanket or hyper-detailed shading.

## Finished print

One vertical 3:5 flat illustration with a continuous clean paper margin. At most one narrow title cartouche containing a short scene-derived title (2–4 Chinese characters, or an exact user-supplied short title). It occupies about 5–10% of image width, sits in negative space and never covers a face or key outline. An optional tiny abstract vermilion seal must stay subordinate; no fake signature, extra date, coordinates or unverified place name. No text paragraphs, gibberish Japanese or oversized typography. Render only the artwork, not a frame on a wall, desk scene, phone or comparison sheet.

## Visual check

One clear subject, flat carved contours, coherent muted palette, actual print-language clouds/water, truthful source structure and cultural identity, quiet frame and whitespace, readable restrained title.

# 双色印刷

Project adaptation of yanliudesign/mono-color-skill, controlled two-ink mode. Original skill, design-system catalogs and MIT license are preserved in upstream/. Upstream example artwork is not bundled or reused. This prompt contains the runtime rules for the postcard format.

## Read and resolve

Identify one recognizable source subject, its mood, key identifying anchors and image role. Preserve identity and factual content while cropping, isolating, enlarging and converting it to mechanical print. Do not invent branded details or replace the subject. Select one composition around this specific photograph, not a fixed template. Make one final vertical 3:5 editorial postcard artwork, not a sheet of alternatives.

## Substrate and ink plates

Use a clean adaptive substrate: Neutral White #FAFAF7 for crisp imagery; Cool Gray #E9E9E5 for architecture; Pale Beige #F5F1E8 for intimate travel and tactile subjects. Never automatically yellow or distress paper.

Use exactly two printing inks with assigned roles. Default Cobalt #2148B8 + Terracotta #C65F38 for travel and leisure; Botanical Green #008A4B + Oxblood #8F3434 for plants; Charcoal #30343A + Signal Red #C83232 for architecture; Mint Green #5EB783 + Charcoal #302D2E for quiet observation. Choose the closest source-appropriate pair and keep it coherent. Dominant ink occupies 70–85% of printed area, accent ink 15–30%. Assign the dominant plate to the main photograph and the accent to selected subject details or title; do not scatter accent shapes. The substrate is not a third ink. Plate overlaps and halftone density are allowed, arbitrary extra colors are not.

## Reproduction and layout

The photograph becomes a printed plate: medium halftone screening, ink pooling and exposed-paper highlights. Maintain clear object contours. Use zero to two subtle controlled imperfections such as mild misregistration and uneven absorption. No digital duotone gradient wash, plastic painting, heavy grunge, antique props or distressed border.

Keep 25–55% visible empty paper, usually 35%, with 5–9% breathing margins. Use one strong focal event and one quiet release region. Choose an asymmetric image-led, specimen, journal or cover layout. One off-center crop or one oversized phrase supplies tension. Travel and leisure should feel relaxed. The hero image should remain large enough to read in a thumbnail; do not shrink it to an insignificant icon or fill whitespace with decorations.

## Type system

Use one short scene-derived English display phrase of 2–8 words unless the user supplies exact wording or requests no text. Preserve provided language. For intimate travel choose literary serif; for urban cultural subjects a clean grotesk; for structured content restrained narrow type. Use at most one secondary utility voice, only when actual supplied information needs it. Place type with deliberate alignment and meaningful contrast. Large type may overlap an uncluttered image edge but must not obscure a face or the main identifying shape. No fake dates, locations, numbers, logos, tiny invented editorial paragraphs or repeated microcopy.

## Visual check

Two inks only; source identity intact; exposed clean paper; actual print screening; one dominant focal event; readable concise type; balanced whitespace. No source-sample composition copying, mockup props, split before/after, device frame or extra postcard border.

# 贴纸手账

Project adaptation of TanShilongMario/visual-memory-translator-SKILL, style_mode=layered_sticker_reassembly. Original skill, selected references and MIT license are preserved in upstream/. This self-contained app preset uses photo input, a single final artwork, and no holiday overlay or style-preview grid.

## Source analysis

Read the actual photograph: main subject, pose, clothing, accessories, foreground, middle ground, distant background and source colors. Select the memory worth preserving. Keep people and objects photographically recognizable; never redraw the person as a cartoon, change their identity or beautify their face. Do not add companions, accessories, landmarks or objects missing from the source.

## Three-layer maximum

Separate at most three truthful photographic fragments: primary subject, a middle-ground fragment and a distant-background fragment. Use two layers if the photograph does not contain three meaningful layers. Keep the source's spatial relationships readable even while changing scale. The main subject is largest; secondary environment is smaller; distant environment is smallest or faintest. Keep a partial body at its honest original crop; do not invent hidden hands, legs or occluded scenery.

Give each fragment a clean warm-white sticker edge, visually consistent and about 2–5% of that sticker's short edge. Use no shadow, or one very faint, short soft shadow. Create distinct separated layers with restrained partial overlap; do not fuse the whole source into one irregular photo sticker and do not repeat the same person across layers.

## Memory-page layout

Make a single flat vertical 3:5 artwork on clean warm off-white art paper with only subtle fibers and no aging. The complete sticker group occupies roughly 25–40% of the canvas area and at least 50% remains open paper. Group the fragments with an intentional asymmetric balance and a clear focal subject. Keep the original visual narrative understandable, while letting the page breathe.

Use one very short poetic title (2–5 words, or a supplied short Chinese title) in quiet serif or restrained handwriting, tucked into a clear paper margin and aligned to the group. If exact wording is supplied, preserve it. No unrelated slogan, long text, fake time/location/serial, signature or decorative metadata. Do not turn the composition into a literal screenshot of an app.

## Avoid

No sticker packs, emoji faces, colorful outlines, decorative tape, paper scraps, torn edges, thick drop shadows, 3D scrapbook effects, repeated subjects, more than three photo layers, collage clutter, full-page landscape repainting or artificially completed hidden content. Render only the finished paper artwork; no desk, hands holding it, external frame, multi-panel comparison or original-photo inset.

## Visual check

Recognizable source person/object, true original pose and crop, distinct clean-edged layers, source-related environmental fragments, generous whitespace, restrained short title and no unrelated decoration.
